title: Priority sprint retrospective and launchpad v0.1
body:
Purpose:
This is a working synthesis following Q4 2025 execution that we will use to (1) capture what actually moved the needle, (2) surface durable learnings for the leadership team, (3) draft a tight set of company-level OKRs for the next quarter, and (4) provide a facilitation-ready run-of-show and announcement draft for the next all-hands.

Scope and framing:
- Timebox: use this doc as the canonical input for the exec prep (Feb 2026) and the company all-hands (first week of Mar 2026).
- Audience: founders/execs, people managers, product leads, and support leads.
- Not a complete postmortem: technical incident postmortems live in SRE. This doc synthesizes cross-org outcomes and planning artifacts.

High level synthesis (one paragraph):
Q4 drove several important platform improvements (batching/caching runway, Dedicated capacity SLA work, and initial Private deployment pilot). We delivered measurable latency and cost improvements for a subset of enterprise customers, but adoption of the new routing controls lagged expectations and we still saw a gap in cross-team rollout discipline (promotions, evals, and rollout measurement). The net: platform stability and cost-efficiency improved, but we under-indexed on developer experience features that accelerate customer onboarding.

Signals and metrics to highlight (quick reference):
- Serving latency p50: 18ms -> 14ms (hosted API, median across curated models).
- Cost per 1k tokens (hosted): -8% quarter-over-quarter after caching changes.
- Dedicated contracts closed: 3 new contracts, combined ARR ~$1.2M.
- Private pilots: 2 customers onboarded to early VPC package; delays due to KMS integration.
- Developer onboarding time (template -> first successful request): median 2.8 days (target 1.2 days).

Top-level learnings (bulleted):
- Shipping infra optimizations moved unit economics but didn’t deliver adoption without tighter DX signals (templates, SDK examples, and onboarding playbooks).
- Rollouts without rollback metrics make teams hesitant to flip defaults; need automated canary metrics and an ops-runbook for rollbacks.
- Sales and Solutions still need a clearer staging story for Dedicated to shorten procurement cycles.
- Quality monitoring (evals + prompt sets) prevented 2 model regressions from reaching production — keep doubling down on this.

Draft company OKRs (candidate set) — feedback required from product & research by 2026-02-20:
Objective A: Make inference predictable and economical for production workloads
- KR A1: Reduce median token cost on hosted by 12% (baseline: end-Q4)
- KR A2: Increase prefix/KV cache hit rate to 42% for top 20 customers
- KR A3: Ship automated rollout canary metric pipeline and run it on 100% of model promotions

Objective B: Drive platform adoption by reducing time-to-first-success for developers
- KR B1: Reduce onboarding time (template->first request) median to 1.0 day
- KR B2: Publish 6 reference deploy/playbook templates for top verticals (SaaS, Healthcare, FinServ, GenAI assistants, eCommerce, Search)
- KR B3: Increase usage from self-serve signups that convert to paying customers by 25% quarter-over-quarter

Objective C: Expand enterprise readiness without adding friction
- KR C1: Close 6 Dedicated contracts (new logos) with SLA commitments
- KR C2: Complete gated KMS/HSM integration and ship as opt-in to Private customers
- KR C3: Improve incident MTTR for Dedicated by 30% with improved runbooks and on-call playbooks

Exec update talking points (for founders):
- What we shipped vs. committed (1 slide each): infra wins, Dedicated backlog, Private pilot status
- Where the gaps are (1 slide): adoption, DX, rollout metrics
- Ask of the execs (one-liners): prioritize launch playbook for Dedicated, approve 2 headcount for onboarding/solutions, and greenlight a 6-week DX sprint after launch

All-hands: facilitation-ready run-of-show (45 minutes + 15 Q&A)
- Timebox: 60 minutes total, aim to be 45 min + Q&A 15.
- 0:00–0:03 — Welcome (CEO) — 1 slide: high-level theme ("From predictability to adoption")
- 0:03–0:08 — Exec highlight (COO) — platform economics snapshot (3 bullets)
- 0:08–0:18 — Engineering demo (Eng VP) — 2 minute demo of new routing dashboard + 1 min on canary metrics
- 0:18–0:25 — Product roadmap (Head of Product) — 3 short items: DX sprint, Dedicated launch plan, Private pilot ask
- 0:25–0:33 — Customer story (Solutions) — short 2-minute narrative + impact numbers
- 0:33–0:40 — People & Ops (People Ops) — hiring priorities & how teams should resource the sprint
- 0:40–0:45 — Close (CEO) — 3 asks to staff and what success looks like by end of next quarter
- 0:45–1:00 — Live Q&A (panel: CEO, COO, Eng VP, Head of Product)

Facilitation notes and props:
- Use the retro-findings slide as an anchor — three wins, three gaps, three asks. Keep slides light.
- Pre-collect questions in Slack #all-hands-questions 48 hours before, and run one internal dry-run with leadership 72 hours before.
- Prepare a one-page TL;DR memo for managers to cascade within 24 hours of the all-hands.

Announcement email draft (manager-facing, short):
Subject: All-hands — "From predictability to adoption" — Mar 3, 10:00 PT
Body: Team, join us for a compact all-hands where we'll share what moved the needle last quarter, what we learned, and three concrete ways every team can help accelerate product adoption next quarter. We'll keep it tight (45 minutes) and leave 15 for questions. If you want your question prioritized, drop it in #all-hands-questions.

Immediate decisions required (list and owners):
- Approve final OKR set (Owner: CEO, deadline: 2026-02-20)
- Approve two temporary hires for onboarding/solutions (Owner: Head of GTM, deadline: 2026-02-18)
- Confirm all-hands date and panel (Owner: Head of Comms, deadline: 2026-02-15)

Open questions / unresolved trade-offs:
- How aggressive should we be with enabling model-variant fallbacks (risk: inconsistent outputs vs benefit: reliability)?
- Should Dedicated pricing include optional onboarding hours or make them billable professional services?
- How to measure adoption velocity in a way that is product-blind (signal vs noise)?

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: DX sprint delays spike onboarding time -> Mitigation: triage backlog to 3 high-impact templates that take <2 weeks each
- Risk: KMS integration slips -> Mitigation: ship partial KMS flow with clear limitations and set customer expectations

Action item tracker (working):
- Priya: Draft final OKRs and circulate to execs (Due 2026-02-12) [linked JIRA: JIRA-4120]
- Marco: Prepare canary pipeline demo and runbook (Due 2026-02-22) [linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/PR-91]
- Linnea: Manager TL;DR and communication toolkit (Due 2026-02-26)
- Samir: Coordinate Dedicated sales playbook and pricing decision memo (Due 2026-02-18)

Appendix (quick references):
- Short list of tickets to review before exec sync: JIRA-4088 (caching rollout), JIRA-3991 (devex templates), JIRA-4022 (KMS blocker).
- Confluence retrospective workspace: https://confluence.internal/redwood/company-q4-2025-retro

Notes to self (working / rough):
- Keep this doc intentionally breathable — aimed at execs and managers, not engineers.
- We will version this doc: v0.1 (working), v0.2 (post-exec feedback), v1.0 (final, published alongside all-hands slides).
- Post-all-hands follow-up plan: 48-hour manager cascade, publish recording + TL;DR, start OKR tracking cadence in team weekly standups.

Unresolved framing (for discussion with founder):
- Do we keep the company theme language 'predictability to adoption' or shift to 'economics + experience'? Quick poll in leadership meeting.
_notes: working document: expect edits, shorthand sections, and open questions. Created as a seed for exec and all-hands planning.
